reviewed_by: Claude review of per-turn elapsed time in the transcript
reason: The transcript never said how long a turn took. Core now records the wall clock from the turn's creation to the message it produced (elapsed_ms on ChatMessage, mirrored on ChatCompletionResponse so a streaming client and a reloaded transcript agree), plus approval_wait_ms summed from the decided approvals bound to the turn's tool calls; a turnless completion falls back to the prepare timestamp. ChatTurnSummary gained started_at so a reload keeps counting from the real start instead of restarting at zero. The transcript shows a counting pill while the turn runs, appends the elapsed to the existing token summary once it lands, adds the elapsed split when that summary is expanded, and reports the duration on a stopped turn. The selection runs test_chat for the timing helper and the persisted message, test_api for started_at on the pending-turn payload, test_harnesses because harness chat turns now persist the same field, and the three frontend suites that own the formatter, the view-model reconciliation and the mid-turn restore fixture.
exclusions: No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No screenshot baselines: the compared snapshots (critical workspaces, zero dark) capture freshly opened workspaces with no completed assistant turn, so the new line never enters them; the elapsed rendering is asserted by text in the assistant journey instead. Playwright is limited to the mocked assistant entries plus the narrow chat-edit-in-place entry, because the changed view model feeds both; the real-core entries are excluded since they need a live Core and this change adds no Core interaction a mock cannot model. tests/test_playwright_impact.py is excluded because ui/playwright-impact.json is unchanged. No full suites.
